gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much of the common 1,200 W state plug-in cap each inverter can use, or what each one would produce and save in a year. One APsystems EZ1-LV fills 75% of the cap (900/1,200). Paired with 900 W of tilted panels in Salt Lake City, it would make about 1,371 kWh a year and save about $182, so its $325 price pays back in about 1.8 years (inverter only, panels extra).
standout_why: I compared five pages. solarwaypoint.com, balconysolarkits.us and pluginsolarcheck.com/kits/certifications already give price per VA for each inverter (EZ1 $0.36/VA, EcoFlow STREAM $0.31/W, Hoymiles 360 $0.41/VA), so cost per watt is not new. solar.com gives PVWatts yearly kWh, savings and payback, but only for a generic 800 W kit. It also lists the 1,200 W caps by state. No page puts those together for each inverter: how much of the cap it fills, how many units you need, and its yearly kWh, savings and payback. solarwaypoint gives only a made-up 183–548 kWh a year that it does not tie to any product.
decides: This supports the EZ1-LV as the one-unit pick: 900 VA uses 75% of a 1,200 W cap and pays for itself in about 2–3 years in a low-rate state like Utah. Only the EcoFlow STREAM Microinverter (1,200 W) fills the whole cap with one box, but its US maker price could not be checked today and its UL 3700 status is listed as 'in progress'. Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV needs 2–3 units to come close to the cap (one 500 VA unit uses 41.7%). That makes it a one-panel or budget choice, not an alternative to the EZ1 for filling the cap.
